concerns.text: The Full-vs-Null model comparison is confounded because the Null Model's model class is unspecified. If the Null Model is also a Random Forest trained on additive features, RFs learn interactions implicitly from raw features, so ΔR² understates interaction effects; if it is linear, ΔR² confounds non-linearity with interaction. The spec must define the Null Model class and acknowledge this limitation, or use a nested/hierarchical design that isolates interaction structure.

FR-004 computes SHAP Interaction Values (which decompose pairwise interactions of the RAW features) while FR-002 also engineers explicit interaction columns (pH_x_salinity) fed to the model. These two signals are not independent: SHAP off-diagonal terms for pH and salinity will largely duplicate the importance of the engineered pH_x_salinity column, so the 'aggregate interaction contribution' double-counts the same effect. The spec should pick one primary quantification and treat the other as a cross-check.

concerns.location: spec.md:SC-001 / US-2 (train/test split) vs Constitution Principle VII
concerns.text: The spec specifies only an 80/20 split with no grouped/leakage-aware splitting. Constitution Principle VII explicitly requires that 'no samples from the same experimental batch or source study appear in both sets.' With pooled public corrosion data, random row-level splits leak study-level artifacts and inflate R². The spec must add a grouped split requirement (e.g., GroupKFold by source study/batch) as a functional requirement.

FR-005 requires permutation-derived p-values for feature importance with BH correction, but never states the null hypothesis being permuted (permutation of the target? of the feature?) or the test statistic (gain in RMSE? SHAP magnitude?). Without this, the p-values are not well-defined. Specify the permutation scheme and statistic.
